(`land/sprint-records`, 2026-09-07, [AGENT]): no concurrent chunk landed a
107 (L3 allocates no number) — THIS entry holds 107; the sprint branch's
"BUG-107" (the `uintptr` repair, `typed-uintptr-identity` @ `5f185fb3`)
exists only in the sprint worktree's staged index and in two whole-file
ledger copies on the archive branch, never on main; it takes the next free
number when (if) L5 is ruled and lands (`docs/2026-09-05_typed-consumer-sprint-handoff.md`,
"BUG numbering reconciliation").

Cause: the crash hook (`_goleanSetupCrash()` — `runtime/debug.SetCrashOutput`
plus the `oracle.registered` acknowledgement) is the FIRST STATEMENT OF
`main`; Go initializes package-level variables and runs every `init()` before
`main` begins, so a subject that aborts during initialization aborts before
the hook exists: both owned files stay empty. Since the channel is MANDATORY
on every classification path (landing review A-R6 — the sprint's first cut
fell through to a raw-marker fallback when ack AND report were both empty,
which made "authenticated" a best-effort claim), the observer refuses:
`crash evidence: no hook registration acknowledgement — the oracle's
_goleanSetupCrash never ran (the subject aborted before main's first
statement, or the hook was not installed); an unauthenticated run is
refused` → FAIL/go-observation. Rows: `init/init-panic` (`init()` panics),
`noodler/initpanic/panic` (same), `noodler/initpanic/var-panic` (a
package-level initializer indexes out of range), `noodler/initpanic/deadlock`
(a deadlock during `init()`); `init/quarantined-var-panicking/sibling` was
already red (FAIL/frontend-export: the frontend refuses the quarantined
panicking initializer) and now fails on the oracle side FIRST, before
frontend export is reached — same cause, a stage change only. The machine's
verdicts on these programs are unchanged and unexamined by the red: an
apparatus refusal never counts as conformance, and never as a machine wrong
answer.

Why red rather than a fallback (the [AGENT] default the brief set, pending
the ruling): the fallback the sprint carried classified pre-`main` aborts
from the raw stderr alone, i.e. from bytes the runtime did not authenticate.
It is stricter than main's old classifier (it counts every marker, with no
continuation exemption) but it is still an unauthenticated read, and a
fallback that fires only when the acknowledgement is empty is exactly the
silent degradation A-R6 named. Fail-closed says: no acknowledgement, no
classification.

The ruling the [USER] is asked for — THREE options (L4 audit fix round,
2026-09-07; the first cut of this paragraph posed only (b) and rejected the
alternative on a false premise — corrected at the end, the auditor's R2):

**(a) Keep RED** — the current default ([USER] direction relayed for L4):
the four `init`/`noodler` rows stay FAIL/go-observation on this line with
the cause written; `sibling` stays red on the oracle side. Honest and
fail-closed; its cost is four authenticated observations Go can in fact
give (see (c)).

**(b) A NAMED pre-`main` exception** — as first written here: an EMPTY
acknowledgement is itself a reliable pre-`main` signal — once `main` starts
the hook cannot fail to write it silently (a failure to open, register or
write exits the child with 78 before the subject runs, and the runner checks
that trailer first), so "acknowledgement empty AND report empty AND the
exit-2 trailer AND a pinned runtime trace" positively identifies "the
runtime aborted before `main`". The exception would (i) require exactly that
state, (ii) classify from the raw bytes under the strict rule (one marker at
a line start, no second marker before the trace, the pinned first frame),
(iii) name itself in the run detail (`pre-main abort (no hook
acknowledgement): raw-marker classification under the strict rule`), and
(iv) be a distinct, tested path — not the fallback the sprint had. It flips
these five rows: the four `init`/`noodler` rows back to PASS and `sibling`
back to its frontend-export red, with no other movement (this chunk's
focused measurement ran every `init/`, `noodler/initpanic/` and
`sync/mutex-unlock-fatal/` row). The auditor RECOMMENDS AGAINST it ([AGENT],
auditor + coordinator): it classifies from raw, UNAUTHENTICATED bytes, and it
re-couples the classifier's correctness to the modeled-surface reachability
argument (a subject cannot forge because `os` is not admitted) that the
landing note §3 now states as a BOUNDARY rather than as a property of the
byte check — the exact coupling the mandatory channel (A-R6) was built to
remove.

**(c) RECOMMENDED ([AGENT] — auditor + coordinator; the ruling is the
[USER]'s): register the hook as a package-level VARIABLE initializer in an
alphabetically-first file, over the fd-passed channel (landing note §3, R1;
§9 item 2), with a generation-time filename guard.** The mechanism, stated
accurately (spec#Package_initialization): «The entire package is initialized
by assigning initial values to all its package-level variables followed by
calling all init functions in the order they appear in the source, possibly
in multiple files, as presented to the compiler» — EVERY package-level
variable of a package is initialized before ANY of its `init()` functions
runs. Among the variables, «initialization proceeds stepwise, with each step
selecting the variable earliest in declaration order which has no
dependencies on uninitialized variables», and «the declaration order of
variables declared in multiple files is determined by the order in which the
files are presented to the compiler» — the `go` command presents them in
lexical filename order, which the spec ENCOURAGES of build systems and does
not guarantee as language. So `var _goleanCrashInstalled =
_goleanSetupCrash()` in an alphabetically-first helper file, whose
initializer depends on no other variable of the package (the hook body
references only its two imports; the identifier is reserved and a collision
refuses), is the FIRST step of the main package's initialization: before the
subject's own variable initializers, and before every `init()`. The auditor
MEASURED it on go1.26.5 (helper `aa_golean_crash.go`): `ack=registered` and
a real runtime-written report for all four shapes on this line — a
package-level initializer panicking (`noodler/initpanic/var-panic` → `panic`
`"init boom"`), an `init()` panicking (`init/init-panic`,
`noodler/initpanic/panic` → `panic`), an `init()` deadlocking
(`noodler/initpanic/deadlock` → `deadlock`). All four become FULLY
AUTHENTICATED observations — no exception, no raw-bytes path, no change to
the classifier's contract — and `init/quarantined-var-panicking/sibling`
returns to its frontend-export red (the frontend's refusal is reached
again). The filename guard: generation REFUSES unless the helper filename
sorts strictly before every other file of the package (`aa.go`, `A.go` and
`00.go` all sort before `aa_golean_crash.go`; a subject file that sorts
first is a named refusal, never a silent reorder) — a `go` command property
pinned and checked, fail closed. Option (c) also RETIRES the `main()` splice
and A-R9's residual outright (landing note §4: the oracle copy then differs
from the semantic input by one added file and no edited byte). HONEST
RESIDUAL: an IMPORTED package's initializer abort still precedes the main
package's variable initialization («the imported packages are initialized
before initializing the package itself») and still refuses with no
acknowledgement — a smaller, exactly nameable class, none of this line's
five rows in it; it stays red by name.

CORRECTION of the first cut ([AGENT], the auditor's R2): this paragraph
previously rejected "registering the hook from a package `init()`" with
«the hook's own initializer cannot be ordered before the subject's other
initializers (Go's initialization order is dependency order; ledger L-011
records it as optimizer-dependent latitude), so an initializer abort could
still precede it». Incomplete on two counts: (1) it considered only an
`init()` FUNCTION — which indeed cannot precede the subject's variable
initializers, since all variables precede all `init()`s — and missed the
variable-initializer placement above, which the same order rule puts FIRST;
(2) L-011 records gc's staticinit PRUNING of the package schedule (an
initializer with no observable effect may be dropped — the
optimizer-dependent latitude), which cannot move a variable initializer
after an `init()`, so it was cited for a claim it does not support. The
rows outside the admitted domain that could ALSO leave the acknowledgement
empty (a subject deleting/rewriting the owned files) remain
`unsupported/frontend-quarantined` at the frontend
(`docs/2026-09-06_observer-crash-channel-design.md`, "Ownership and
configuration boundary"); under the fd-passed channel they also lose the
path.

Repro: `func probe() int { var fs []func() int; for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
fs = append(fs, func() int { return i }) }; return fs[0]() + fs[1]() +
fs[2]() }` under a `go.mod` declaring `go 1.21`: `go run .` (go1.26.5)
prints **9**, GoLean returns **3**. Change only the directive to `go 1.26`:
both print 3. The pinned toolchain honours the module's language version
(the loopvar change, Go 1.22); we do not.

Cause: `tools/nativefrontend/langversion.go` sets `types.Config.GoVersion`
from the embedded pinned-toolchain table, never from the module context, so
a directory carrying an older module directive is ACCEPTED and its meaning
changed. `docs/spec-sources.md` already names the language version as
semantics, not packaging (the pin's third leg).

FIXED ([AGENT] S2, 2026-09-12; `tools/nativefrontend/modfile.go`): the nearest
`go.mod` at or above the lowered directory — and, for every case-local
imported package, at or above ITS directory (a nested `go.mod` is its own
module) — is located the way the go command finds a module root, and its `go`
directive's language version (`go/version.Lang`, so `go 1.26.0` and `go
1.26rc1` are `go1.26`) must equal the pinned one (`langversion.go`
`pinnedLangVersion`, derived from the embedded toolchain table = the oracle
pin). Otherwise the export REFUSES by name in the ruled form: `<path>/go.mod
declares go 1.21; GoLean implements the Go 1.26 language only (…)`. Also
refused by name: a `go.mod` with no `go` directive (the go command then
assumes go 1.16 — another language version), a repeated or malformed
directive, an unparseable version. No `go.mod` anywhere above → the pinned
1.26, unchanged (the corpus's mode: zero `go.mod` files under `Corpus/`,
verified; `raftharness/go.mod` declares `go 1.26` and governs no lowered
directory). The directive is read by a small strict scanner (stdlib only, no
x/mod; `//` comments stripped, `require ( … )` blocks skipped) that refuses
what it does not understand rather than guess. Movement: none — no corpus row
carries a `go.mod`; the raft twin wire is byte-identical. OUT OF SCOPE,
recorded as owed: `//go:build go1.N` per-file constraints (already refused as
reserved tags by `langversion.go`), `//go:debug` lines, the `godebug` go.mod
directive (added [AGENT] 2026-09-15 per audit N1,
`docs/2026-09-15_review-boundary-audit.md`: e.g. `godebug default=go1.21` is
accepted silently — case g12 — and is inert under the oracle's
`GO111MODULE=off`), and the `toolchain` directive (inert under the oracle pin
guard's `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`). The
frontend's refusal formats are classified for `scripts/lower-diagnose`
(`tools/lowerdiag/causes.tsv` row `foreign-module-version`, by-design). The
original fix sketch follows.

Ruling ([USER] Mike 2026-09-11, relayed: refuse non-1.26): this semantics implements the Go 1.26 language only. Fix: when
the lowered directory — or an imported source package — carries a `go.mod`
whose `go` directive's language version (major.minor) is not 1.26, REFUSE
by name at export (`go.mod declares go 1.21; GoLean implements the Go 1.26
language only`). [AGENT] detail: no `go.mod` → the pinned 1.26, unchanged
(the corpus's mode). Per-file `//go:build go1.N` constraints and
`//go:debug` settings are out of this entry's scope.

## BUG-114 — the abort observer REFUSES a gc sample of a wake-then-abort program when a SECOND report boundary (`panic: `, `fatal error: ` or `runtime stack:`) appears after the selected panic origin — a terminal-race report shape (main exiting while the worker's panic prints) the crash-channel classifier does not model; exposure-dependent (1 of 80 draws at the slow tier's K=80; 0 of 32 at the gate's K=32) [apparatus; terminal classification; trusted surface #2; found by train r45's `ci --slow` at `74d084ad`, 2026-09-21]

- Pinned-by: none (the exposure is a sampling event, not a deterministic row state: `goroutines/wake-then-abort` PASSES at K=32 (`scripts/diff-one`, 2026-09-21, «enumerated=2 exhibited=1 draws=32») and passed every earlier `--slow` run at K=80; the refusal appeared at draw 61/80 of round 45's slow run and is recorded in `docs/evidence/2026-09-20_unseq-stage-d/README.md` (train r45). Reproduce: `GOLEAN_SLOW=1` membership sampling at K=80 (or higher) on the row until a draw's stderr carries a second boundary.)

What happened: `draw 61/80 (plain) go sample: could not extract Go panic message: abort classification:
additional or unknown report boundary after selected origin, refused; stdout="{…\"status\":\"ok\",
\"values\":[{\"kind\":\"int\",\"tag\":\"int\",\"value\":42}]}" stderr="panic: worker abort in the pr…"` — the
observer's `crashview.go` (~121) refuses when the tail of the authenticated report AFTER the selected
origin contains another `panic: `, `fatal error: ` or `\nruntime stack:` (A-R6: no unauthenticated
read; a second boundary means the report is not one attributable abort). The program
(`Corpus/coverage/exec/goroutines/wake-then-abort/main.go`): a worker sends on a buffered channel then
panics in its private segment; main receives and exits — the L5 exit-window latitude. On this draw gc's
stderr carried, after the worker's `panic:` report, a second boundary — the shape is consistent with
main's exit racing the runtime's panic printing (the report interleaved with the exit path's own
output), but the FULL stderr was NOT preserved: the coordinator overwrote `artifacts/coverage/latest.tsv`
with a focused re-run before copying the reason line (disclosed; the classification text above is
exact, the stderr tail is truncated at the harness's snippet width). The machine's certified set for the
row is unchanged ({panic "worker abort in the private segment", 42}).

Why it matters: an apparatus refusal is a FAIL by doctrine (never a pass), so a K-dependent exposure
turns a certified-green row red on the slow tier at random — noise that hides real drift. The gap is
COVERAGE of gc's concurrent-exit report shapes in the observer, not a machine or oracle disagreement
(same family as BUG-106 fatal-during-unwind and BUG-107 pre-main abort: report shapes the
authenticated channel cannot attribute).

Fix plan ([AGENT]): capture the full stderr of a refusing draw (run the row at K=200 under
`GOLEAN_SLOW=1` with the harness's raw-stderr retention), classify the exact second-boundary shape
against the runtime's `printpanics`/`exit` interleaving (`deps/go/src/runtime/panic.go`,
`proc.go`), then EITHER extend `crashview.go`'s attribution to that shape (with a positive control and
a forgery control, per the L4 observer rules) OR, if the shape is genuinely unattributable, keep the
refusal and move the row's exposure into a named apparatus limit (a `params` note + this entry's
Cases line). Observer changes are trusted surface #2 → their own lane, audit ask unconditional.

Capture (2026-09-21, [AGENT] worker, lane `records/bug114-capture-0921`; RECORDS ONLY — no observer
code changed; evidence `docs/evidence/2026-09-21_bug114-capture/`): **the second-boundary shape was NOT
reproduced on the row.** 73,600 recorded draws (45,600 plain, 28,000 `-race`) plus 1,140 smoke draws —
74,740 total — over 11 configurations (the generated oracle package, the gate's exact environment
`GO111MODULE=off GOFLAGS= GODEBUG=panicnil=0 GOTRACEBACK=system`, a freshly truncated
`oracle.crash`/`oracle.registered` per draw; GOMAXPROCS 1/2/4/8 sequential and unset (=32) under 8- and
16-way concurrency; both the built binary and the gate's own `go run .`): **0 draws whose authenticated
report carried a second `panic: `, `fatal error: ` or `runtime stack:`.** Three outcome classes only,
all with exactly one boundary — abort with the `ok 42` JSON on stdout (the class draw 61 was in:
13081/32000 plain, 1996/9600 under `go run`), abort with no stdout, and a CLEAN exit 0 with empty stderr
and empty crash file (57/9600 under `go run`, never with the bare binary). No truncated report was
observed in any draw. Per-draw exposure, rule of three, one-sided 95%: <= 6.6e-5 on plain draws
(3/45,600), so P(a K=80 slow run reds on this row) <= ~2.6e-3 (~1 run in 380) under ISOLATED conditions —
plainly not the gate's regime (the one event occurred inside a `GOLEAN_MEM_MAX=48G scripts/capped
scripts/ci --slow` run with the slow-tier enumerator saturating the box); with a single observed event
the gate-conditions rate is not estimable to better than an order of magnitude (at p = 6e-4 / 2.5e-3 /
1e-2 per plain draw the per-slow-run risk is 2.4% / 9.5% / 33%). Box-wide memory pressure was NOT
manufactured to chase it — the box is shared with other lanes.

Classification against the pin (go1.26.5, `deps/go` @ `c19862e5f8`): the three boundary tokens have
exactly these printers — `panic: ` in `printpanics` (`panic.go:747`) and in `gopanic`'s four
bad-context guards (`panic.go:820,827,833,842`, each followed immediately by a `throw`); `fatal error: `
in `throw` (`panic.go:1224`) and `fatal` (`panic.go:1248`); `runtime stack:` in `dopanic_m`
(`panic.go:1587`), only when the crashing g IS the M's g0. All are on the terminal path, which is
serialised by `startpanic_m` case 0 (`panic.go:1530-1538`: `m.dying=1`, `panicking.Add(1)`,
`lock(&paniclk)`, `freezetheworld`) and `dopanic_m`'s `unlock(&paniclk)` / `panicking.Add(-1)`
(`panic.go:1604,1606`), and all printing is under the global `debuglock` (`print.go:59,69`) so reports
concatenate and never interleave. Therefore **a token after the selected origin's trace header means a
SECOND terminal event began printing after the first report's traceback**, in one of two sub-shapes:
(a) a second complete report from another M that was parked on `paniclk` — two independent origins,
genuinely UNATTRIBUTABLE, the refusal is correct; (b) a same-M continuation — a `throw` on the M that is
already printing (`m.dying==1`) prints `fatal error: <msg>` and then `startpanic_m` case 1 prints the
literal line `panic during panic` (`panic.go:1544`) — one origin, ATTRIBUTABLE. Shape (a) was exhibited
and the gate's refusal text reproduced byte for byte on a throwaway probe (eight goroutines panicking
together; `probe-two-abort.report`, two complete reports in one crash file), with two real row draws as
the positive control (`refusal-repro.txt`). **Shape (b) was NOT observed and is named from the source,
not from a capture.** For THIS row shape (a) with a second `panic: ` is not reachable from the program
text (one panic site; the generated `main` can only panic if the stdout JSON encode fails, and stdout is
a regular file under the gate), so a second terminal event here must be runtime-internal — but which
token draw 61 carried is NOT DETERMINED, and this lane does not guess it.

Consequence for the fix plan above: it still stands, but **the interim "a `params` note" is not
implementable as written** — `scripts/diff-coverage`'s `parse_lane_params` fails closed on any key

## BUG-118 — `cap([]rune(s))` for a NON-LITERAL `s`: the machine's pinned singleton cap = len was OUTSIDE gc on almost every input — gc realizes the 32-rune conversion buffer (`[32]rune`, every non-literal operand of ≤ 32 runes, written or not) or roundupsize(4·len)/4 (escaping, or > 32 runes); len itself is a member only when 4·len is a size class [semantic core; wrong answer (observed ∉ modeled); FIXED by the R3 / b6 widening `ChoiceSite.convCap` (lane `lane/conv-cap-1007`, 2026-10-07); known since the 2026-08-19 rune arm's own comment («cap([]rune("héllo")) = 32», deliberately left unpinned), measured as a wrong answer by the b6 design note's 140-row envelope (`docs/evidence/2026-10-07_conv-cap-design/envelope.tsv`)]

- Status: fixed ([AGENT] build worker, lane `lane/conv-cap-1007`, 2026-10-07; the widening ratified [USER] Mike
  2026-10-07 (agreed; build approved), relayed — design `docs/2026-10-07_conv-cap-design.md` D1–D8, under the standing rule that semantic widenings must match real Go: the envelope is EXACTLY gc's measured member set)
- Pinned-by: differential
- Cases: strings/conv-cap/runes-var-nomut-5, strings/conv-cap/runes-var-esc-5, strings/conv-cap/runes-var-nomut-33, strings/conv-cap/runes-var-esc-33, strings/conv-cap/runes-var-nomut-100, strings/conv-cap/runes-var-esc-100
- Discovered: 2026-08-19 as a transfer caveat (triage L1, the `runesFromString` arm's comment and latitude inventory
  R3's rune paragraph: «gc is outside the singleton even on the small NON-escaping shape … a cap-observing case was
  measured red and deliberately NOT added»); classified a WRONG ANSWER (not a latitude caveat) by the b6 design note
  (2026-10-07, §1 correction (ii)); born red-first on this lane (`docs/evidence/2026-10-07_conv-cap/red-first-witness.txt`:
  modeled `{5}`, gc 32 plain and `-race`, for `runes-var-nomut-5`; modeled `{5}`, gc 6, for `runes-var-esc-5`)

WHAT: spec §Conversions to and from a string type declares the capacity of `[]rune(s)` implementation-specific
(«may be larger than the slice length»). The 2026-08-19 arm pinned the SINGLETON cap = len with no choice
consumption, and recorded that gc disagrees on the small non-escaping shape — but did not pin the disagreement as a
case, so the wrong answer lived in a comment. gc go1.26.5 (`walk/convert.go` `walkStringToRunes`,
`runtime/string.go` `stringtoslicerune`/`rawruneslice`, `runtime/msize.go` `roundupsize`): a NON-literal operand of
n ≤ 32 runes converts into the 32-rune stack buffer whether or not the result is written (there is no rune
zero-copy regime), an escaping result or n > 32 allocates `roundupsize(4n)` bytes — so `cap` is 32 for n ≤ 32
non-escaping, `roundupsize(4n)/4` otherwise (6 for n = 5 escaping, 36 for n = 33, 104 for n = 100); the length is
realized only for a LITERAL operand (`stringtoruneslit`) or when 4n is itself a size class
(for n ≤ 32: n ∈ {0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32} (and every n > 32 with 4n a size class)). Every non-literal rune conversion whose cap is observed (directly, or
through an `append`'s aliasing) was therefore a wrong answer on `main`.

FIX (this lane, design D1–D4): the two conversion heads draw `ChoiceSite.convCap` at the strict apply over
`convCapMembers kind literal n` (Ops.lean) — the measured union of gc's regimes per (kind, literal?, len): runes
non-literal `{roundupsize(4n)/4} ∪ {32 | n ≤ 32}`, bytes non-literal `{n} ∪ {roundupsize(n)} ∪ {32 | n ≤ 32}`,
literal `{n}` — nothing in between. The default tape's rune slot 0 is the size-class member (gc's deterministic point
for n > 32, its escaping point below); the byte slot 0 is `n` (the zero-copy member, the pre-widening singleton — no
byte row's observation moves). The six rune rows above are born red-first and PASS at the lane tip — the two at n = 5
as membership rows (envelope {6, 32}), the four at n ∈ {33, 100} as STRICT rows (their envelope is the singleton
{36} / {104}, which the membership lane refuses by design; on `main` they are plain differential mismatches, 33 vs 36
and 100 vs 104 — the witness file records the pre-change membership-shape run: modeled {33} / {100} vs gc's 36 /
104); the byte rows `strings/conv-cap/bytes-*` witness every byte member likewise (not a wrong answer on `main` — the
singleton `n` was a gc member for every byte conversion — but the membership lane's singleton guard made them red
there too).

- Status: open
- Pinned-by: differential (PINNED 2026-10-12, lane `fix/release-runtime-1012`, release-readiness item 1 — [USER]
  Mike 2026-10-12 (starting with the items that need no input from the user), relayed by the [AGENT] coordinator: the

- Neighbourhood: S4 (identity, equality and nil-ness) — swept 2026-10-26, lane `sweep/s4-identity` ([AGENT], campaign plan §4). The operand and binding routes beside `ident-var`/`ident-lit`: a CONSTANT operand, a package-level string variable, the two conversions bound to PARAMETERS (a variable and a literal operand), a SUBSTRING operand (`&b[1] == &c[0]` for `c := []byte(s[1:])`), a second variable holding the same string — gc `true`, the machine `false` on each: six red rows added to the Cases line above (`strings/sweep-s4-conv-identity/bytes-{const,global-var,params,params-lit,substring,copied-var}`, this entry's own mechanism, so no new number); controls that agree: `[]rune(s)` twice (gc always allocates), an ESCAPED result, the round trip `[]byte(string(b))`, two conversions of two CALL results (rows `runes-twice`, `bytes-escaped`, `bytes-roundtrip`, `bytes-call-operand`, PASS at birth) — 10 cells (`.tmp/probes/conv-*`). The other routes (map key, box, `switch`) are n/a: a slice is observable only by nil-ness and element addresses; the race route is reads only on both sides. Cells left: none; the mechanism (`convCapApplyAt`: a fresh backing per conversion) is unchanged and the disposition stays the owner's (R19).
- Discovered: 2026-10-07, the conv-cap lane's Fable adversarial audit (verdict MERGE-CLEAN; this its item 1, a
  pre-existing wrong answer, not introduced by the lane), as relayed by the [AGENT] coordinator; rowed by the [AGENT]
  train worker r74 — every detected gap is rowed, [USER] Mike 2026-09-03, relayed.

WHAT: spec §Conversions to and from a string type gives a `[]byte(s)` result no freshness guarantee, and gc realizes
sharing: under the zero-copy regime (`escape/escape.go` `OSTR2BYTESTMP`, a non-literal operand whose result is never
written and does not escape) the slice ALIASES the string's bytes, so two such conversions of the SAME string share one
backing; two `[]byte("hello")` literal conversions also compare equal under gc (that mechanism not separately
diagnosed). Element-address
identity observes it, in-language (no `unsafe`):

```go
func mkA(n int) string { s := ""; for i := 0; i < n; i++ { s += "a" }; return s }
func identVar() { s := mkA(5); b := []byte(s); c := []byte(s); println(&b[0] == &c[0]) }
func identLit() { b := []byte("hello"); c := []byte("hello"); println(&b[0] == &c[0]) }
```

gc go1.26.5 prints `true` for both, under the default build, `-gcflags=-l` and `-race`; the machine (`golean
native-json-run` on the frontend's wire, main's binary as built by train r73) prints `false` for both — observed ∉
modeled (`docs/evidence/2026-10-08_train-r74/bug121-repro.txt`; the auditor's own probe was the scratch
`.tmp/audit-cc/ident.json`, pruned at train r74's close). The capacity axis (R3, `ChoiceSite.convCap`) does NOT
cover this: the zero-copy member's aliasing is unobservable through WRITES (gc takes zero-copy only when nothing
writes), but element-address identity is a separate, unmodelled axis — the four «unobservable» claims (R3 in the latitude inventory, the
conv-cap design note twice, the `convCapMembers` docstring in `Ops.lean`) were corrected to say so at train r74, and the
inventory rows the axis as R19.

WHERE: `GoLean/GoCore/Machine.lean` `convCapApplyAt` (every conversion allocates a fresh backing); the latitude
inventory R19.

FIX PLAN (NOT scheduled; a widening is a future [USER] decision under the standing rule that semantic widenings must match real Go, [USER] Mike 2026-10-07, relayed): model the shared-backing member (an identity choice at the zero-copy
regime, read-only by construction), or keep the fresh-allocation pin and record the deviation as an R15-style
version-tracked red row. Fix criterion: a corpus row over the program above PASSES with gc's `true` in the modeled set.

  backlog authority (starting with the items that need no input from the user) and the standing rule [USER] 2026-10-07
  that semantic widenings must match real Go, relayed — every added member is gc-witnessed; design
  `docs/2026-10-12_sched-boundary-design.md`)
- Pinned-by: differential
- Cases: goroutines/sched-dependent/len-peer-send, builtins/print/goroutine-gap
- Discovered: 2026-10-12 by the review (F1: a NEW counterexample; R2: the FR-30 class recorded 2026-09-05 as silently
  admitted, re-witnessed). Reproduced on the lane at the base tip `d92b95fd` with the review's two witnesses
  (pinned gc go1.26.5, GOMAXPROCS=2): `len(c)` witness — machine DFS `{0, 11}` (18,368 steps) and dedup `{0, 11}`
  (18,121 nodes, `certified=checkCert`), gc plain 9999/1/0 and `-race` 9861/72/67 for 0/1/11 over 10,000 calls, no
  race diagnostic; print witness — machine DFS `{ACB, BAC}`, gc plain ACB 993 / ABC 7 and `-race` ACB 891 / ABC
  107 / BAC 2 over 1,000 calls.

WHAT: `Config.atBoundary` (`GoLean/GoCore/Multi.lean`) decides where the pool's scheduler may switch goroutines —
registry ops, spawn, exit, the parked shapes, the post-op flag, loop back-edges; between boundaries a goroutine's
steps are «private to it». Two operations are not private: the channel arm of `lengthOf` (`Machine.lean`) reads the
channel cell's buffer count — shared state a peer's send or receive changes with no synchronization required
(spec#Channel_types, spec#Length_and_capacity; the memory model orders a send before the completion of the
RECEIVE only) and with no access footprint (gc's `chanlen` is uninstrumented, latitude inventory U2; `NPDRF.lean`
obstruction 5 names exactly this «empty recorded footprint» hazard) — and the `print`/`println` apply writes fd 2,
the observable (gc's `printlock` serializes one STATEMENT; ledger FR-30). With no boundary at either, a peer's send
could not land between two reads and a peer's print could not land between two prints: the model's scheduling
relation admitted fewer runs than gc realizes, with no refusal — a silent wrong answer surviving projection to a
returned integer (the `len` case) or to the byte output (the print case).

FIX (this lane; design note §2–§3): two SHAPE arms of `Config.atBoundary` — the `len` apply on a channel operand
(`.retV (.chan _) (.strictK (.lengthOf _) _ [] _ _)`) and the print apply (`.retV _ (.stmtOpK (.print _) _ _ [] _ _)`)
— consulting the existing L1 site (goroutine-order menu; a sole runnable pops nothing, so sequential conservation
is untouched); neither sets the post-op flag (neither completes a registry op); a pre-boundary at every observable
operation realizes every cross-goroutine order of observable events. NOT boundaries, by argument: `cap(ch)` (a
channel's capacity never changes), `len` of a map (an instrumented read — a concurrent write is a detected race),
`len`/`cap` of a slice/array/string (private value reads), pure computation (the witnesses' `delay` recursion). No
new choice site, no change to `schedSlots`/`Config.boundarySite`/the post-op rule; no pinned statement's text
changed (`stepML_switch_boundary` names `t.atBoundary` by name; the frozen pool surface does not define it); every
proof that unfolds the predicate is shape-insensitive and went through unchanged. The two rows above are the
witnesses as membership rows pinned to the widened sets `{0, 1, 11}` and `{ABC, ACB, BAC}` (members=3 each); gc's
extra members are rare per draw (≈ 0.7 % each for `len`, ≈ 10 % / 0.2 % for the prints under `-race`), so the
`members=` pin is usually not reached at the gate budget — a caption, never the result. FR-30 is CLOSED by the
print arm (`docs/language-coverage-ledger.md`). Canonical-stream consequence recorded in the design note §2: at the
new consults the default stream's slot 0 is the lowest-index runnable goroutine, so a child at a print or `len(ch)`
beside a runnable main now yields to main where it used to continue — strict rows are stream-invariant by their own
check, so no result depends on it.

WHAT: spec#Numeric_types makes `uintptr` a distinct type («an unsigned integer large enough to store the uninterpreted
bits of a pointer value»), identical to no other type (spec#Type_identity). `GoLean/NativeToIR.lean` `intKindOfName`
maps the wire's `uintptr` to the machine's `.uint64`, so after decoding the two types are one identity. Every runtime
comparison of identities then collapses them (gc go1.26.5 on the left, the machine at the lane base `4365c313` on the
right — the review’s reproduction block re-run at the lane base `4365c313` (a run dump is reproducible from the tree and is not committed, `docs/evidence/README.md`)):

| expression | gc | machine |
|---|---:|---:|
| `any(uintptr(1)).(uint64)` comma-ok | false | true |
| `any(uintptr(1)) == any(uint64(1))` | false | true |
| type switch over `any(uintptr(1))`, `case uint64: 64; case uintptr: 1` | 1 | 64 |
| `len(map[any]int{uintptr(1): 7, uint64(1): 9})` | 2 | 1 |
| `any([]uintptr{1}).([]uint64)` comma-ok | false | true |
| `any(&uintptrVar).(*uint64)` comma-ok | false | true |

inventory §11 item 6); arithmetic, conversions, storage, `atomic.*Uintptr`, `println` lower and pass as before

refused at the CLI's observation seam (`GoLean/CLI.lean`, the kind table has no `uintptr`) — that refusal protects the
observation channel only, not a boolean or int computed from the identity, which is what the six probes return.

THIS ENTRY'S CELLS: D2–D5, D7–D9: a method-only `main`, `main` with a parameter, a result or type parameters, `init` with type parameters, `main` as a var or a type, `main` redeclared across files, a function redeclared across files (rows `functions/main-{method-only,with-param,with-result,type-params,declared-var,declared-type,redeclared-across-files}`, `functions/func-redeclared-across-files`, `init/init-type-params`); `main` as a CALLEE on four routes — BUG-220 (not rowable: the harness drops `func main` from a subject).

WHAT: the frontend is a SUBJECT lowerer — the machine's entry is the CLI's `--function <name>`, and the differential
corpus's exec directories are `package main` files WITHOUT `func main` by design (the oracle harness generates the
`main` around the subject; 436 of the 1396 `package main` directories under `Corpus/coverage/exec` have no `func main`, measured 2026-10-12). So the frontend has no
notion of «a whole program gc would build», and the gc check «function main is undeclared in the main package» (made
by cmd/compile, not go/types) has no counterpart. No wrong answer follows from it today: running the wire with
`--function main` is the machine's named error (`entry function not found: main`); any other entry runs a function gc
never ran as part of this (rejected) program, which is the subject mode's contract, not an observation of the program.

WHY NOT FIXED IN-LANE: the smallest frontend check («package main declares no func main» at load) would refuse every
subject-mode export of the exec corpus; the real fix is a whole-program MODE (a flag the negative leg passes, or a
manifest-driven entry contract) — a frontend-contract design question, not a few lines. Fix criterion: the
negative-corpus row `functions/main-undeclared` PASSes on the frontend leg (`frontend=type-check` or a named
whole-program refusal) with no exec-corpus row moving.

FIX (2026-10-13, [AGENT] lane `frontend/main-undeclared-refuse-1013`), under the [USER]'s ruling on the options
(a whole-program mode vs a refusal), Mike 2026-10-13, relayed by the [AGENT] coordinator: (refuse the case rather than open the door to special-casing; support may come later). So the defect — the frontend LOWERED a program gc rejects — is fixed by refusing it, not by a mode:
- by default (no flag) the frontend refuses a `package main` whose checked package declares no `func main`, right
  after type-checking, as `nativefrontend: type-check: function main is undeclared in the main package (<dir>; …)`,
  exit 1, no wire (`tools/nativefrontend/entrymode.go`, one call in `load.go`). gc's text is its linker's
  (`runtime.main_main·f: function main is undeclared in the main package`) and carries NO source position — measured
  at the go1.26.5 pin on the row, on a two-file package and on a package whose only `main` is a method; so the
  refusal names the directory, not a file. A non-`main` (library) package is not subject to the rule (gc requires
  none); a non-function `main` is go/types' own error, before this check.
- `--subject` (new flag) skips exactly this check — the differential corpus's mode, where the oracle harness
  supplies `main` around the subject. Every apparatus exporter of a corpus subject passes it (`scripts/diff-coverage`
  both lanes — `scripts/diff-one` goes through it —, `membership-sampling`, `detector-soundness`,
  `choice-trace-corpus`, `tools/admission-check.py`); `scripts/coverage-negative` passes nothing (whole program).
  Callers whose inputs always declare `func main` are unchanged (the wire-boundary and unseq-wire fixtures, the
  frontend-pins twin and deviation case, the raft tools' assembled programs, cedar-census drivers, gotest-triage's
  `$GOROOT/test` programs). `scripts/lower-diagnose` and `tools/lowerdiag report` gain the same `--subject` knob;
  the static judge applies the same rule (cause row `main-undeclared`, by-design, export scope).
- NOT owed: a whole-program MODE (lowering such a package's other functions as gc never would run them) is the
  ruling's deferred support; no further gc compilation-unit rules are mirrored on this account (ledger §5.1 item 7). Fix round (train 9, the lane's pre-merge review, MEDIUM-1): an `unsupported` refusal's «full blocker picture» pointer line, and the two doc sentences, carry `--subject` when the export did — without it `lower-diagnose`'s first refusal is this rule, not the blocker (demonstrated on `constants/typed-complex-binary`); NIT-2: `lowerdiag report`'s note for this key names the entry rule instead of the body/initializer boilerplate; LOW-1 (a `func main` only in a build-constraint-excluded file is refused by file selection first, under BUG-108's posture) recorded in `entrymode.go` and ledger item 7, not changed; LOW-2 (the `type-check:` label on a link-time error) kept as is, honest by its parenthetical.

WHAT: gc's rule (cmd/compile/internal/noder/writer.go funcDecl): a body-less function is rejected («missing function
body») when the package is compiled `-complete` — cmd/go passes it when the package has no non-Go files, and the
frontend's file selection already refuses non-Go sources, so every admitted directory is `-complete` — unless the
function is `//go:linkname`d (a directive in a file that imports "unsafe"; gc rejects the directive elsewhere) or
`//go:wasmimport`ed (honoured only when GOARCH is wasm — never at the pinned linux/amd64). go/types accepts the
declaration; the frontend stubbed it as `unsupported: bodyless function f` and lowered everything else.

WHY IT IS NOT BUG-125: BUG-125 is the absence of a whole-program MODE (a main-less `package main` is the exec corpus's
subject contract); this one is a per-declaration rule gc applies regardless of entry — a whole-program rejection
needs no mode.

FIX: `tools/nativefrontend/gclimits.go` (the post-type-check hook of release-readiness row 34) rejects the program as
`type-check: <pos>: missing function body` for every body-less function or method of a source unit that is not
linknamed by such a directive (the stub quarantine stays for linknamed declarations). `go/ast` finds 0 body-less
declarations under `Corpus/`, `raftsubject/`, `raftharness/`; no exec row moves. Pinned by the negative row and
`TestGcSizeLimits` (d01, d02, e02, g11, g13). CORRECTED 2026-10-13 (BUG-127, lane `frontend/directives-1013`): a user
`//go:linkname` now refuses at FILE SELECTION, before this rule, so the linkname exemption is unreachable for user
units and was removed; g11 and g13 moved to `TestCompilerDirectives` as directive refusals.

comment whose text begins `go:` to the pragma handler, in any column; `//line` at column 1 and `/*line` anywhere
rewrite positions). go/types accepts the program and the lowering never sees the comment, so the effect vanishes
with a clean export: `//go:embed data.txt` + `var x string` — gc fills `x` from the file (prints 5 for «hello»), the
model seeds the zero value and answers `0`, status ok; with data.txt absent gc rejects the package («pattern
data.txt: no matching files found») and the frontend still exported it. `//go:linkname x runtime.zerobase` +
`var x uintptr` (file imports "unsafe") — gc's linker rejects («link: main: invalid reference to runtime.zerobase»),
the frontend exported and the model answered `0`. A verb gc does not know is IGNORED outside the standard library
(noder.go: the «not allowed» error is std-only), so an unknown `//go:foo` is inert in gc; refusing it is over-refusal
in the fail-closed direction.

WHAT: the go command folds GODEBUG settings into a binary's defaults (cmd/go/internal/load/godebug.go
defaultGODEBUG): the main module's go.mod `godebug` lines, then the `//go:debug` lines of package main's files, on
top of the defaults for the module's go version — and a module with NO go.mod (GOPATH mode, the corpus's mode) gets
the pre-1.21 defaults. `panicnil` is the setting that changes a modeled program's meaning: under `panicnil=1`
`panic(nil)` is recovered as a nil value, under the Go 1.21+ default it is a `*runtime.PanicNilError`. The model
implements the modern semantics only (the machine's panicPayload; emit.go emitPanicStmt's note), and the
differential runner pins the oracle with `GODEBUG=panicnil=0` on every `go run` (scripts/diff-coverage, the
arc-final audit F21 of 2026-08-06) — a contract that lived in a runner comment and the latitude inventory, nowhere a
consumer reads. The frontend's strict go.mod scanner (modfile.go, BUG-109) skipped a `godebug` line
(`fields[0] != "go"` continued past it) and took `godebug (` for a block whose body it skipped; `//go:debug` lines
were never read.

RED FIRST (measured 2026-10-13, this lane, gc go1.26.5): with GODEBUG unset and no go.mod, the review's program
(`//go:debug panicnil=1`; `recover() == nil` after `panic(nil)`) prints `true` in gc; the frontend from main
2e69dd86/084267be exported it and the model answered `false`, status ok. `//go:debug nonexistentSetting=1`: gc
rejects («invalid //go:debug: unknown //go:debug setting "nonexistentSetting"»), the frontend exported, the model
answered `7`. The corpus row `directives/debug-panicnil`: gc `true`, model `false`; under the runner's pin
`GODEBUG=panicnil=0` gc prints `false` too (the environment overrides the source directive), so the differential
runner would have MASKED this delta — the row's value is the pinned refusal. The defaults, same program WITHOUT
any directive: GOPATH mode (GO111MODULE=off, no go.mod), GODEBUG unset: `true` (LEGACY); the same with
`GODEBUG=panicnil=0`: `false`; inside a `go 1.26` module (GO111MODULE=on): `false`; that module with
`godebug panicnil=1` in go.mod: `true`. Main's frontend accepted a go.mod `godebug panicnil=1` line and a
`godebug (` block silently (exit 0, a wire written); the lane's refuses both by name.

FIX ([USER] Mike 2026-10-13 (item 3 agreed), relayed): `//go:debug` is refused by the directive scan
(`tools/nativefrontend/directives.go`) in ANY user unit at ANY position — the go command honours only package main's
pre-package-clause lines; refusing the rest over-refuses by name — as `… carries the runtime-setting directive
\`//go:debug …\` — GODEBUG settings are not modeled: the semantics is the Go 1.26 module defaults (panic(nil) raises
*runtime.PanicNilError; the differential oracle is pinned with GODEBUG=panicnil=0) …`; a go.mod `godebug` line or
block is refused by the strict scanner (modfile.go goDirective) as `module directive: <go.mod> sets godebug (…) — …`,
in every go.mod the scanner reads (gc honours only the MAIN module's; a nested module's is over-refused by name).
No setting is modeled. THE CONTRACT, now stated in `docs/cli.md` §1 («Runtime defaults») and `docs/release.md` §4:
the model is Go 1.26 module-mode semantics; `panic(nil)` is `*runtime.PanicNilError`; the oracle is pinned with
`GODEBUG=panicnil=0`; a consumer comparing a wire's run against gc by hand must run gc with the same pin (or inside
a `go 1.21`+ module with no godebug override), else the `true`/`false` difference is the oracle's configuration,
not the semantics. Static twin: causes.tsv `runtime-setting` (by-design, export scope). Pinned by
`TestCompilerDirectives` (three `//go:debug` shapes), `TestModuleGoDirectiveRefusal`, the Cases row and the
negative row.

FIX ROUND (2026-10-13, review MEDIUM-2 and LOW-4, relayed): the scanner MISSED the `godebug(` spelling (no blank
before the paren), which gc honours (measured: a go.mod with `godebug(` / `panicnil=1` / `)` prints `true` under
`GO111MODULE=on GOPROXY=off`; the first landing's frontend exited 0 on it — `fields[0] == "godebug"` saw
`godebug(`). x/mod's lexer makes `(` and `)` tokens of their own (cmd/vendor/golang.org/x/mod/modfile/read.go), so
the scanner now splits them off before reading the verb, and is STRICT: gc's go.mod grammar at the pin
(modfile/rule.go, the verb switch) is enumerated in `modfile.go` goModVerbs — `module`, `require`, `exclude`,
`replace`, `retract`, `tool`, `ignore` accepted (line or block: the module graph cannot reach the lowered program,
whose imports are the pinned GOROOT's stdlib and case-local relative paths; `tool`/`ignore` steer the go command,
never the compiled program), `go` judged (BUG-109), `toolchain` accepted only when it names the pin (`go1.26.5`;
another name is refused — under GOTOOLCHAIN=auto a consumer would build with an unmeasured toolchain; the
apparatus runs GOTOOLCHAIN=local, where the line is inert, measured on `toolchain go1.27.0`), `godebug` refused
(line, block, `godebug(`, a trailing comment, `godebug default=go1.20`), any other verb refused by name (gc: «unknown
directive: frobnicate», measured). Pinned by `TestModuleGoDirectiveRefusal` (one case per spelling). THE CONTRACT,
completed (LOW-4): (a) the oracle runs in GOPATH mode, where the go command applies the go 1.16-era defaults to
EVERY GODEBUG setting (`gover.DefaultGoModVersion = "1.16"`, cmd/go/internal/modload `MainModules.GoVersion` with no
module; `godebugForGoVersion`), and the runner pins only `panicnil`; the contract coincides with the oracle because,

register: runtime's `containermaxprocs`/`updatemaxprocs` touch GOMAXPROCS only, math/rand's `randseednop` needs

— so every future admission carries the obligation stated in `docs/stdlib-admission-register.md` («GODEBUG
obligation»); (b) `go.work` `godebug` lines are a THIRD override the frontend never reads: measured, a workspace's

WHAT: spec#Comparison_operators — «Two struct values are equal if their corresponding non-blank field values are
equal» — and gc agree that a blank field's operand is never STORED: `cmd/compile/internal/walk/complit.go` `fixedlit`
assigns the element to `_` and `cmd/compile/internal/compare/compare.go` skips blank fields in the generated equality.
The native frontend emitted every positional operand into the `struct-lit` (`tools/nativefrontend/emit.go`
`emitStructLit`, and the unseq sweep's twin `unseq_lower.go` `structLitHead`), so the value carried the operand and the
core's `valueEqFields` (`GoLean/GoCore/Ops.lean`), which compares every declared field by name, read it — in `==`, in
map-key identity and in the comparability check that panics on an uncomparable dynamic type. Four pre-existing corpus
cases hold blank fields (`structs/blank-field`, `noodler/structs`, `spec-examples-stmt/struct-tags`,
`spec-examples-decl/compile-only-forms`); none compares them, which is why the baseline stayed green.

THE FIX (lowering only; `GoLean/` untouched): at a blank field `_ T` of a positional literal the field takes T's zero
value, on both lowering paths (`emitBlankFieldZero`, called by `emitStructLit` and by the unseq sweep's
`structLitHead`), so equality, map keys and copies follow from the core's unchanged comparison. The 11 original Cases
rows were RED at the branch base (the wrong booleans, counts and the two panics) and PASS since; `plain-variable-read`
and `pkg-init-plain` (2026-10-14) pin the admitted non-constant operand. Keyed literals cannot name a blank field (gc
and go/types: «unknown field _ in struct literal» — the negative row `structs/blank-field-keyed`, PASS at
`frontend=type-check`); an omitted blank field already took the zero value. Anonymous non-empty struct types are
FR-13's standing frontend refusal, so no literal of one reaches this lowering.

THE OPERAND — the 2026-10-13 lowering EVALUATED it (an `index-get(array-lit …)` discard wrapper at the field's
position; the sweep lowering it for its occurrences), and the lane's pre-merge review (relayed) measured two classes
where gc's observation lies outside that model's set, both pre-existing at the base: (F1) gc DROPS a side-effect-free
blank operand together with its run-time panic, (F2) gc never evaluates a package-level literal's blank operand at all.
The disposition is the [USER]'s ruling of 2026-10-14 and the record is BUG-130's: the operand is NOT evaluated; a
constant, nil or a plain variable read gives the zero value, anything else refuses the literal by name.

## BUG-132 — the `sortSlice` machine op records EVERY window element as WRITTEN, so a concurrent READ of a slice being sorted is refused `race` where gc's pdqsort on an already-ordered window (or suffix) performs no write and `go run -race` is green [semantic core, race-detector footprint; over-refusal (the machine refuses ⊇ gc), a status-level differential observation; found by the pre-merge adversarial review of lane `frontend/g19-sort-intercept-1025` (F1, relayed by the [AGENT] coordinator), 2026-10-25; recorded as a red pin pending the owner's ruling]

- Status: open
- Expect: FAIL
- Pinned-by: differential
- Cases: race/sort-op/sorted-window-concurrent-read
- Discovered: the reviewer's program `s := []int{1,2,3}` with the sort in one goroutine and `seen = s[0]` in
  another: the lane answers `status=race`, main (the generic path at the time) answers `ok 1 1 2 3`, and
  `go run -race` is green. Entry: [AGENT] lane worker, 2026-10-25 (the review's F1, relayed).

WHAT the op does (`GoLean/GoCore/Machine.lean`, the `.sortSlice` apply arm, unchanged by the re-admission): the
visible window is read (`Mem.loadSlice`: one `.data` read per element), sorted, and written back in full
(`Mem.storeRun` from visible index 0: one `.data` WRITE per element) — the write set is the whole window
whatever the input order. WHAT gc does (`deps/go/src/slices/zsortordered.go` @ go1.26.5): `pdqsortOrdered` on
a window of at most 12 elements runs `insertionSortOrdered`, which swaps only out-of-order neighbours — an
already-ordered window, or the ordered suffix of one, is never written; longer windows take the pattern-
breaking and partition paths, which write what they move. So a read concurrent with the sort races in the
machine on the elements gc leaves untouched. The machine's verdict (`status=race`) is a differential
observation: the row's expected status is `ok` and the row FAILS at `lean-observation` with the cause
`race:race`. DIRECTION: fail-closed — the machine refuses a race-free program; it never answers `ok` where gc
reports a race (a write the op records that gc also performs is a true race on both sides). NOT NARROWED:
restricting the recorded writes to the elements that change would be unsound the other way — pdqsort may
write an element it leaves in place (a swap chain through it, the partition's moves), and a write the machine
drops is a false `ok` under a concurrent read. The faithful set would be pdqsort's own, which is what the
retired generic path realized (the control row `race/sort-op/sorted-window-concurrent-read-generic`: `go
slices.Sort(s)` is the function value, the generic, race-free in both). The 2026-10-25 ruling (backlog row
50, option 1) accepted the op as the default lowering for the sorted result's uniqueness; this entry records
the class the detector's verdict adds, for the owner's ruling. raft's `slices.Sort` sites sort LOCAL
temporaries (`CommittedIndex`'s stack array, `Slice`/`Visit`/`VoterNodes`/`LearnerNodes`' fresh slices,
`String`'s copies) that no other goroutine reads: unaffected. Latitude inventory C10, alignment fact (iii).

WHAT WAS WRONG. `sliceCapBudget` (BUG-090) bounds the element COUNT of a `make` and the decoder's
`checkMakeFootprint` (BUG-078 (2b)) bounds count × footprint only for a CONSTANT count read off the wire; a
count computed at run time — a variable, a parameter, an expression — passed both and `buildDefaultArrayValue`
materialized count × leaves `GoValue` nodes. Past the box's cap that is a cgroup kill the runner records as
`killed:137` (a non-verdict, honest but not a refusal, and not reproducible on a machine without `capped`,
where it is an OOM).

THE GUARD (`GoLean/GoCore/Machine.lean`, the `makeSlice` arm of `applyStmtOpCore.plan`): after gc's own
`makeslice` panics (a request gc rejects keeps gc's panic text) and after the `sliceCapBudget` refusal (a count
past it keeps that refusal), before any backing is built, `cap × tyLeafCount(elem) > arrayFootprintBudget`
refuses by name — `make([]T, len L, cap C): a slice backing of C elements of F scalar elements each materializes
C·F scalar elements, past the interpreter's footprint budget for a run-time-length make (16777216 elements,
arrayFootprintBudget — the constant-length form refuses at decode, checkMakeFootprint; BUG-131 cost boundary,
refused by name)`. The budget constant MOVED to the core (`Machine.arrayFootprintBudget`, beside
`sliceCapBudget`; `NativeToIR.arrayFootprintBudget` reads it, `tools/nativefrontend/budgets.tsv` transcribes it
and `budgetsTableTests` pins the transcription — one number). The element footprint is `tyLeafCount`
(`GoLean/GoCore/Ops.lean`), the decoder's `tyFootprint?`/`typeDefFootprint?` restated over the machine's type
table on the `tyHasPointers` descent: `[n]T` is n × T's leaves, a struct the sum of its fields (at least 1), a
defined type its underlying's, everything else one leaf; it refuses exactly where `tySizeBytes` (read first in
the arm) already does. The unit is LEAVES, not bytes ([AGENT] 2026-10-25): the backing is a tree of one

- Discovered: the equality/identity review of train 19 (`docs/reviews/2026-10-26_equality-identity-review.md`
  F1, branch `review/equality-1026`; probes `p31`, `p33a`–`p33s` beside it): with `type A struct{ X, Y int };
  type B struct{ X, Y int }; a := A{1, 2}; pb := (*B)(&a)`, every WHOLE-VALUE route through `*pb` refused
  `stuck` — `*pb == B{1, 2}` («left struct equality type mismatch: expected main.B, got main.A»), `x := *pb`,
  `any(*pb)`, `m[*pb]`, `switch *pb`, `eqB(*pb)`, `i.(B)`, and the store `*pb = B{9, 9}` («struct value type
  mismatch: expected main.A, got main.B») — where gc prints the answer; only the leaf-field routes worked
  (BUG-133's rows, triage L7). The same class was found once before and ROWED but never fixed: the C1
  memory-module audit's F9 (2026-09-18) is ledger frontier FR-34 / queue 34, whose proposed red-first rows
  were never written. Reproduced by this lane at the base `6e05137a` exactly as the review gives it (17
  probes `stuck`, `p33k`'s value-conversion control green), then widened to the local space below: 57 of
  the 60 rows born RED at the base.
- Neighbourhood: S2 (conversions: a missing kernel arm or a value not retagged) — swept 2026-10-26 by
  lane `sweep/s2-conversions` (plan §4, [USER]-approved 2026-10-27). THE MATRIX: every target kind of
  `convertValueToTy` and the emitter's routes (int, float, string, `[]byte`, `[]rune`, struct, array,
  pointer, slice, map, func, interface, chan, bool, sync, type parameters, defined-over-defined, typed
  nils) × the routes (explicit, constant, conversion of a call, chained, literal element / field / key,
  return, assignability without a conversion, box, method receiver, the deref read, nil) × the sites
  (the kernel's arms, `normalizeValueForTyAt`, `derefRetag` / `receiverRetag`, `structTagCompatible`'s
  field arms, the emitter's dedicated operators, the bool strip, the interface wrap, the constant
  fold): 118 cells — 74 PROBED by this lane (28 probe packages, two of them refusal probes; gc
  go1.26.5 = the machine on every legal one), 35 COVERED by existing rows or the train-20 /
  equality-review probes (cited per cell in the lane's report), 9 OUT OF SCOPE by a refusal named at

  kernel's `.interfaceDecl` / `.opaque` arms, unreachable from a type-checked wire; cross-package

  (bools 4, constants 6, strings 12, structs 22, multipkg 1, pointers 11, conversions 15, channels 2,
  assign-order 7, generics 6, methods 5, interfaces 3, sync 2), strict, expected = gc, all PASS.
  FINDINGS: none — no wrong value, no wrong panic, no `stuck` on a legal program. CELLS LEFT: the
  nine out-of-scope refusals above (coverage gaps by name, not defects) and BUG-134's two recorded
  residuals (an address target carries no static type, release-readiness row 57; unexported field

WHAT (the base): a `Loc` carries no static type, so a `.base` load (`loadLoc`, Ops.lean) returns the cell's
value under its MINT tag, and the `.deref` apply (`applyStrictOp`, Machine.lean) delivered that value as
is: `*pb` evaluated to `.struct main.A …` at static type `B`. Every value-level consumer then compared the
tag against the static type and refused — `valueEq`'s struct arm (`leftType != name`), and
`normalizeStructValueWith` (reached from `Store.alloc`, `bindParams`, the map-key and boxing
normalizations and `storeLoc`'s leaf write `writeAt` at the cell's DECLARED type, so a `B`-tagged value
refused into an `A` cell — the store never happened, hence no retagged cell and no wrong answer). Triage L7
(2026-08-19) had relaxed exactly the three FIELD checks (`fieldGet` and the field arms of
`loadLoc`/`writeAt`) under `structTagCompatible` and said so; the whole value was never in scope.

THE FIX — one predicate, two sites, the cell keeps its mint tag (`GoLean/GoCore/Ops.lean`,
`GoLean/GoCore/Machine.lean`):

- `TypeEnv.structTagCompatible` (identical wire `FieldDef` lists — spec#Conversions' struct-tag clause,
  the L7 rule) is now the ONE predicate behind every tag-compatible site; `structTagCompatible ctx` is it
  at `ctx.types`, and the field arms are unchanged.
- `retagStruct types name v`: a struct value whose tag differs from `name` but is tag-compatible with it
  takes the tag `name`, fields untouched; anything else is returned unchanged. This is Go's conversion
  between the two named types — a value of identical underlying type under the other name, no run-time
  effect in gc — so it is observationally the explicit conversion the type checker requires, and a tag
  that is NOT compatible is untouched and refused downstream exactly as before.
- THE READ SIDE: the `.deref ty` apply returns `derefRetag ctx ty x` — when the pointee's static type `ty`
  resolves to a struct type tag-compatible with the loaded tag, the value is retagged to it. Go's `*pb`
  HAS type `B`, so every route downstream (`==`, assignment, boxing — the box carries dynamic type `B` —,
  map keys, `switch`, parameter binding, the type assertion, the readout's type name) sees `B`. The
  narrowed-read footprint (`projChainTarget`) and the access trace are untouched. The same read for a
  VALUE-RECEIVER method dispatched through a pointer (`receiverAt`'s `.deref` adjust: a `*B` box, a
  promoted `(*T).M` expression) is retagged at the method's receiver type (`receiverRetag`, at the
  three dispatch sites — `dynamicDispatch?`, the promoted method-expression entry, `preprintDispatch`,
  which now also refuses by name a pending target with no declaration instead of carrying it to the
  entry); the frontend lowers the STATIC call `pb.Sum()`, the method value `pb.Sum` and the value box
  `var j Summer = *pb` with an explicit `deref`, so only the pointer-box dispatch needs it.
- THE WRITE SIDE (placement per the train-20 audit's F1, 2026-10-26 — the first version of this fix put
  the retag in `normalizeValueForTyAt`'s struct arm, i.e. at EVERY normalization site): the write through
  an ASSIGNMENT TARGET — `storeTarget`'s chain (`x = v`, `*p = v`, `p.f = v`, `a[i] = v`) and the unseq
  lane's binder write of a frozen-target read (`unseqLoad`) — is `Mem.storeThrough`: the STRICT store
  first (`Mem.store`, the leaf normalized at the cell's declared type, every refusal by name), and only
  when it refused and `cellRetag?` names the value under the cell's DECLARED struct type (a tag-compatible
  struct — the converted-pointer case) the write of that retagged value; any other refusal is the strict
  store's own, verbatim (an incompatible tag is never absorbed). `cellLeafTy` is `writeAt`'s own
  `Ty.stepDown` descent on the type. `Store.alloc` (declarations), `bindParams` (parameters), the map
  key/value, channel-element and literal normalizations are STRICT: `normalizeValueForTy` refuses a
  tag-compatible mismatch by name exactly as at the base, so the audit's hand-edited wire `p10` (a
  `var b B` initialized by an `A`-tagged literal, no conversion) stops at the declaration with «struct
  value type mismatch: expected main.B, got main.A» — pinned, with the conversion routes beside it, by
  `Tests/GoCoreEval.lean` `structRetagBoundaryFacts`.
- THE RESIDUAL (recorded, not hidden): at a store through an assignment target the pointer's static
  type is not on the wire (an `addr` target carries no type — `targetPlan` gives `*p = v` and `x = v`
  the same `TargetRef.chain`), so `Mem.storeThrough` is tied to the only route a real conversion can
  reach rather than to the conversion itself: a forged wire whose RHS at a target store carries a
  compatible-but-different tag is retagged there (status `ok`) where the base refused it. A type-checked
  wire cannot produce that (go/types requires the RHS type to be the target's static type, which is the
  cell's declared type unless a pointer conversion intervened). ITS WIRE-LEVEL SCOPE, measured: a
  DECLARATION WITH AN INITIALIZER lowers as the zero cell plus an assignment (`var b B = e` and `b := e`
  are `.assign (.var b) e`, NativeToIR's `var` arm), so the auditor's hand-edited `p10` wire still
  answers `ok 12` at this tip (base: `stuck`), exactly as it would under the auditor's own sketch (the
  `writeAt` leaf) — the narrowing removes the absorption at parameters, map keys and values, channel
  elements, literal fields and elements, `append` / `copy` and at `Store.alloc` itself (the hand-built
  `p10` shape, pinned), not at the initializer store. Closing the residual needs the target's static type
  on the wire or a `TargetRef` constructor for address targets (`*p`, `p.f`, `a[i]`) distinct from the
  variable chain — a frontend + decoder + `TargetRef` change (226 sites), raised for a separate lane.

WHAT IT DID NOT CHANGE: BUG-133's identity semantics (`valueEq`'s pointer arm, `Loc.canon`; the 44
`identity-*` rows stay green); Go's dynamic-type rule for interface boxes (`any(*pb) == any(*pa)` is
`false`, `any(*pb) == any(B{1, 2})` is `true` — the box is built from the retagged value, so the rule
decides on `B` vs `A` exactly as Go: rows `value/boxed-type-differs`, `shapes/iface-dynamic-type`,
`shapes/defined-over-defined`); the leaf-field routes (L7); `valueEq`'s struct arm (unchanged — it never
sees a mismatched tag from a deref now); the normalizer (strict, as at the base); the cell's mint tag
(`HeapNormal` holds: the stored value takes the declared tag); the kept statements (`scripts/gen-contract
--check`: no regeneration — `next_storeK_chain` / `next_storeK_var` keep `storeLoc … = .ok s'` as their
hypothesis, under which the strict store succeeds and `Mem.storeThrough` IS that store); the race
detector's keys (one write event either way); the frontend and the wire. Proofs repaired, statements
unchanged: `applyStrictOp_wf`'s deref arm (`derefRetag_locSup`), `storeTarget_pres` / `unseqLoad_pres`
(`Mem.storeThrough_eq` / `_pres` / `_shape`: one `Mem.store` of a value with the same loc bound),
`preprintDispatch_locSup` and `dynamicDispatch?_locSup` (`receiverRetag_locSup`), the G16 set
(`TableMono.derefRetag_eq`, `cellLeafTyFrom_eq`, `cellLeafTy_eq`, `cellRetag?_eq`, `receiverRetag_eq`,
`Mem_storeThrough_eq`; `preprintDispatch_mono` through `findFunctionIn?_mono`), the error-class leaves
(`Mem.store_tame`, `Mem.storeThrough_tame`, `Mem.storeThrough_noPanic`); new lemmas `retagStruct_self`,
`retagStruct_locSup`, `cellRetag?_locSup`. (`isNormalForTyAt_sound` is textually unchanged — the
first version listed it in error, audit F3.)

STATUS WORD (the review's point (i)): the refusal was honest about its cause and wrong about its class —
`stuck` is defined as «outside the lowering contract (a frontend bug)» (`docs/semantics-overview.md` §8),
and these programs are legal Go the frontend lowered correctly. With the fix no refusal remains on the
class; the texts «struct value type mismatch» / «struct equality type mismatch» still name a tag that is
NOT tag-compatible — a frontend fault, which is what `stuck` means. BUG-133's survey sentence
(«ACCESS through either spelling already worked») is amended there to say «for leaf fields».

KNOWN LIMIT OF THE PREDICATE (train-20 audit F2, low): `TypeEnv.structTagCompatible` compares wire
`FieldDef` lists, and the wire carries a field NAME without its declaring package, while
spec#Type_identity makes same-spelled UNEXPORTED field names from different packages different — so
`sub.A{x int; Y int}` and `main.C{x int; Y int}` read compatible here although `(*C)(pa)` is illegal.
The frontend's go/types pass rejects the conversion («cannot convert pa (variable of type *sub.A) to
type *C», the auditor's `p11-cross-pkg-negative`), so no type-checked wire reaches the
over-approximation; it widens the residual above to cross-package pairs on a forged wire. Closing it
needs the package on unexported field names (a wire change: frontend + decoder), out of this lane; the
auditor's negative program is not in the negative corpus — adding it is the negative-corpus lane's
(this lane was told to stay out of that corpus), raised at the stage.

- Discovered: the equality/identity review's F2 (low), 2026-10-26, probe `p15-nil-left` (eleven `println` lines
  over every operand kind plus a tagless `switch` case; gc prints them, the base frontend quarantined the
  subject). Entry: [AGENT] lane worker `frontend/workspace-and-oracle-1026`, 2026-10-26.

WHAT (`tools/nativefrontend/emit.go` emitBinary): a comparison carries its operand type on the wire, taken
from the LEFT operand (`operandTypeExpr = b.X`) and switched to the right only when the right side is the
interface of a mixed interface/non-interface comparison (BUG-017). go/types records a bare `nil`'s type as
`untyped nil`, and emitType has no arm for it (`wire.go`: `unsup("basic type %s", b)`), so `nil == p` for a
pointer, map, slice, func or channel right side — and the `case nil == np:` of a tagless switch — quarantined
the whole subject. `nil == i` for an interface or error right side already took the right side's type through
the mixed-comparison rule and lowered; in the review's probe it was quarantined with the rest of the function
by the first bare-nil comparison.

RED FIRST (measured at the base 6e05137a): the review's p15 — gc prints its eleven lines; the base frontend
exported the program with `run` quarantined and the machine answered `unsupported`, message
`frontend-quarantined: basic type untyped nil`. The corpus rows: six subjects `unsupported` at the base
(pointer, map, slice, func, chan, switch-case), the interface and error subjects already `10110` / `11001`.

FIX: when the left operand's recorded type is untyped nil and the right's is not, the operand type is the
right side's — the type of the comparison, exactly what `p == nil` carries (`isUntypedNilType`). THE LOCAL
SPACE: both sides untyped nil is a type error go/types refuses before emission, with gc's own text («invalid
operation: nil == nil (operator == not defined on untyped nil)», measured on both sides, the frontend's
type-check stage); an untyped CONSTANT on the left — `1 == x`, `"a" == s`, `1.5 == f`, `true == b`,
`'a' == r`, `3 == m` for a defined int, `1 == iface`, `2 < x`, `"b" > s` — is recorded by go/types with its
converted type and already lowered (measured on both sides: `true true true true true true true false true
true`); `nil == e` for an `error` and `nil == i` for `any` were already right (the two control rows). At the
tip every row PASSes with gc's values (`110 10110 10110 10110 10110 11001 10110 10010`: the nil-left
spellings score exactly as their nil-right twins).

SITE: `GoLean/GoCore/Machine.lean` `panicPayload`; `scripts/diff-coverage` `go_run_oracle` (the pin). ROUTE: `panic(nil)` recovered or aborting; the typed-nil payload (`panic((*T)(nil))`) was unaffected and is the control.

- Discovered: 2026-10-26, the S4 sweep's matrix cells «zero-size × elements / fields» (probes `.tmp/probes/zs-{array-elems,slice-elems,fields-adjacent,fields-final-pair,fields-separated}` of the lane, both sides): gc go1.26.5 `true` on every element and adjacent-field pair, stack or heap; the machine `false`, status `ok`, no refusal. Entry: [AGENT] lane worker, 2026-10-26.
- Neighbourhood: S4 (identity, equality and nil-ness) — the finding of this shape's sweep (lane `sweep/s4-identity`, 2026-10-26); its own neighbourhood is the matrix cell it came from: arrays (stack, heap, through a pointer, boxed), slices (`make`, escaped, `[][0]int`, a literal, as map keys), struct fields (adjacent at offset 0, adjacent after a non-zero field — the padded final pair —, boxed, escaped, as map keys): the 14 red rows above; the controls that agree: zero-size fields SEPARATED by a non-zero field (`&s.A == &s.B` false: different offsets) and the padded final field of two distinct NON-ESCAPING variables (false: BUG-170's stack member) — rows `fields-separated`, `final-single-distinct-vars`, PASS at birth. The VARIABLE cells (escape-driven) are BUG-170's. Cells left: none.

WHAT: spec#Size_and_alignment_guarantees — «Two distinct zero-size variables may have the same address in
memory» — with spec#Variables (the elements and fields of a structured variable each act like a variable) and
spec#Comparison_operators («Pointers to distinct zero-size variables may or may not be equal») leave the answer
open; gc's realization for ELEMENTS and FIELDS is address arithmetic, not an allocation decision: element `i` of
an array or slice of a zero-size type is at `base + i·0 = base`, a zero-size field at its layout offset, so two
adjacent zero-size fields share one offset, and a zero-size FINAL field is padded to stay inside the object
(`cmd/compile/internal/types/size.go`), which is why `N int; A, B zsT` has `A` and `B` at one offset after `N`.
The member is the same on the stack and on the heap — unlike R15's VARIABLE case (BUG-170), where only the heap
member coincides (`runtime.zerobase`). Measured on gc go1.26.5 (the rows above): `var arr [3]zsT` → `&arr[0] ==
&arr[1]` true, `&arr[0] == &arr[2]` true; `make([]zsT, 3)`, `[]zsT{{}, {}}`, `make([][0]int, 2)` → true; `type adj
struct{ A, B zsT; C [0]int }` → `&s.A == &s.B` true; `type lead struct{ N int; A, B zsT }` → true; through `any`
boxes the same; `map[*zsT]int{&s[0]: 1}` then `m[&s[1]] = 2` → one entry. The control `type sep struct{ A zsT; N
int; B zsT }` → `&s.A == &s.B` false (offsets 0 and 8) on both sides.

SITE: `GoLean/GoCore/Ops.lean`, `valueEq`'s pointer arm compares canonical PATHS (`l.canon == r.canon`, BUG-133);
a `Loc` carries no size and no offset, so `.index b 0` ≠ `.index b 1` and `.field b "A"` ≠ `.field b "B"` whatever
the element or field size; `mapEntryIndex?` (the linear `valueEq` scan) and the interface arm reach the same arm,
so the map-key and box routes follow. `Store.alloc` allocates the aggregate as one cell with per-element and
per-field sub-paths: zero size is not a notion of the store or of the path.

FIX SHAPE (for the owner's ruling; not this lane's — a sweep lane does not fix core code): what gc exhibits for
elements and fields is a FUNCTION of the layout, not a choice — two paths into ONE root cell denote one address
exactly when their byte offsets agree — and `tyStructLayout` / `tySizeAlign` (Ops.lean, oracle-pinned against
`unsafe.Offsetof` / `Sizeof`) already compute field offsets and element sizes, so the pointer arm could decide two
paths with the same root and a zero-size pointee by offset (every element of a zero-size element type sits at the
array's offset; a zero-size field at its layout offset), keeping distinct roots distinct — the VARIABLE case stays
BUG-170's two-member envelope (same / fresh), routed to the membership lane. Alternatively the whole zero-size
address space becomes one envelope with gc's member inside. Fix criterion: the 14 rows above PASS with gc's
values and the two controls stay green; BUG-170's rows are untouched by it.
