WHAT: `execProgLoop` / `execProgLoopOut` (`GoLean/GoCore/Multi.lean`, the `mainOutcome? = some` arm: `match runnableIdxs … with | [] => return out`), mirrored by `enumPoolRun` and `poolDFS` (`GoLean/CLI.lean`), `poolLoop` (`GoLean/ChoiceTrace.lean`), `nodeObs` (`GoLean/EnumDedup.lean`) and the checker's `EnumDedupCheck.lean` — seven sites of one arm. `runnableIdxs` filters by `threadRunnable`, whose parked case is `wakeReady`, the Bool projection of `wakeReady?` that reads an `.error` (a channel block on an unbound address or a non-channel cell, a sync cell of the wrong shape) as `false`. At main's exit the empty menu was taken as «nothing left to run» and the run was `ok`; the L5 exit window (`ChoiceSite.l5ExitWindow`, bound 2) is not offered either, so a schedule decision was also taken on the absorbed error (with a runnable goroutine beside the malformed one the window IS offered, over a menu the malformed goroutine is missing from). Away from main's exit the same empty menu is `deadlockOrRefusal`, which re-checks every parked goroutine (`parkedWellFormed`) and names the first malformed one — BUG-165's fix, which stopped one arm short. BENIGN VALUE: `ok` with main's readout and the folded output prefix. WHAT A REFUSAL SHOULD SAY: `wakeReady?`'s own error — the load's text (`chanPayload?`'s «unbound GoCore heap location», a cell-shape «expected channel data …») or `.internal` on the op/cell shape mismatch — the text `deadlockOrRefusal` already raises for the same state one arm away. REACHABILITY: hand-built state only — no wire node parks a goroutine on an address `Store.alloc` never wrote (DC11's own analysis, BUG-133's lane); not reachable from Go source; a forged wire cannot name a parked configuration. FIX (landed 2026-10-27, the DC11 pattern): `exitOrRefusal` on the `[]` arm in ONE definition the seven sites and the checker share (the Status line has the site table), the three pinned facts flipped to the named refusal, the controls kept; the proof-side copies (`PoolFacts.front`, `execProgLoop_unfold`, `checkCert_complete_aux`) follow the arm.

## BUG-207 — `runeAt` / `runeSizeAt` at an offset AT OR PAST the string's end ANSWERED U+FFFD and width 1 instead of refusing: `decodeRuneAt`'s out-of-range sentinel (a byte value outside every accept range) is Go's rule for a sequence truncated INSIDE the string and was the same benign answer for a malformed offset — LATENT (the lowering guards the offset; the op is not a wire node) [semantic core; latent absorbing default on the trusted surface, the BUG-085 class; found by the S26 sweep 2026-10-26, lane `sweep/s26-core-defaults`; FIXED 2026-10-27 in lane `core/fix-bug206-207-1027` — the two strict arms refuse the offset by name]

- Status: fixed (2026-10-27, lane `core/fix-bug206-207-1027`; the campaign plan's rule that a finding is fixed through the normal train, [USER] approved 2026-10-27, relayed. MECHANISM: `GoLean/GoCore/Machine.lean` `applyStrictOp`, the `.runeAt` and `.runeSizeAt` arms — after the existing negative-offset refusal, `if (str.length : Int) ≤ off then stuck "rune decode offset {off} out of range for a string of {str.length} byte(s)"`; `decodeRuneAt` (`Ops.lean`) and its two self-guarding callers (`runesOfStringAux`, `utf8StringAux?`) are unchanged, so the in-range behaviour — including the truncated-sequence sentinel, the spec's rule — is byte-identical (the corpus: every row unchanged under `scripts/ci --diff`). Proof repair: `applyStrictOp_wf` (`StateWf.lean`), one more `split` per arm for the new refusal; `applyStrictOp_tame` and `applyStrictOp_eq` discharge the arm unchanged. No equation lemma states these arms (`Equations.lean` states `applyStrictOp`'s `.toInterface` arm only); no kept statement changed (`scripts/gen-contract --check` clean, no regeneration).)
- Pinned-by: none (LATENT — no corpus row can reach the arm: `for i, r := range s` lowers to `if rnext >= len(s) { break }` before `runeSizeAt`/`runeAt` at `roff = rnext` (`GoLean/NativeToIR.lean`, the range-over-string lowering), and `.runeAt`/`.runeSizeAt` are synthesized by the decoder there, never carried by the wire. The pins are `Tests/GoCoreEval.lean` `absorbingDefaultResidualFacts`, since the fix asserting the refusal: `applyStrictOp .runeAt ["ab", 5]`, `.runeSizeAt ["ab", 2]` and `.runeAt ["", 0]` are the «out of range» `stuck` — beside the controls: in range `'b'` decodes, the truncated `"a\xE2"` at offset 1 is U+FFFD with width 1 (Go's rule), and a negative offset keeps its own refusal.)
- Discovered: 2026-10-26 by the S26 sweep (lane `sweep/s26-core-defaults`), reading `decodeRuneAt`'s `.getD 0x100` (`GoLean/GoCore/Ops.lean`) against its three callers.
- Neighbourhood: found by the S26 sweep (the shape's inventory is on BUG-165); its own neighbours — the other two decoders over the same sentinel, `runesOfStringAux` (string → `[]rune`) and `utf8StringAux?` (the abort renderer) — guard `off < s.length` themselves and are not exposed.

WHAT: `decodeRuneAt` (`Ops.lean`) reads bytes as `((s.bytes[off + i]?).map (·.toNat)).getD 0x100` — a sentinel outside every accept range, so a sequence truncated by the END of the string decodes as U+FFFD with width 1, `unicode/utf8`'s rule for an incomplete encoding and the oracle-pinned range-over-string behaviour (`strings/range-invalid-utf8`). The same sentinel at `off ≥ s.length` made the strict ops `.runeAt` / `.runeSizeAt` (`Machine.lean` `applyStrictOp`, which refused only a NEGATIVE offset by name) answer `(0xFFFD, 1)` on a MALFORMED operand — an offset no decode position has — where `utf8.DecodeRuneInString(s[len(s):])` answers `(RuneError, 0)` and no Go construct decodes there. BENIGN VALUE: `.int 0xFFFD .int32` / `.int 1 .int`, values a hand-built program prints or compares as if decoded. WHAT A REFUSAL SHOULD SAY: `stuck "rune decode offset {off} out of range for a string of {n} byte(s)"` at the two strict arms' operand check, beside the existing «negative rune-decode offset» refusal; `decodeRuneAt`'s in-range sentinel stays (it is the spec's rule inside the string). REACHABILITY: hand-built state only. FIX (landed 2026-10-27): the operand check at the two arms exactly as stated, the two pinned facts flipped to the refusal (plus the empty string at offset 0), the controls kept; `decodeRuneAt` and its guarded callers unchanged.

## BUG-216 — a `// +build` line go/build does NOT honour — under a `//go:build` line, not followed by a blank line before the package clause, inside a `/* */` block, or after one — is judged as a constraint by the frontend's own comment scan, which REFUSES the export saying the oracle would compile without the file, while gc INCLUDES the file (its init runs: 2); a misnamed over-refusal of a legal program, no wrong answer [frontend boundary; the BUG-155 scan against go/build's header rule; found by the S20 sweep 2026-10-27, lane `sweep/s20-admission`; FIXED 2026-10-27 in lane `frontend/fix-admission-1027` — the header rule is go/build's own, ported line for line]

- Status: fixed (2026-10-27, lane `frontend/fix-admission-1027`; the campaign plan's rule that a finding is fixed through the normal train, [USER] approved 2026-10-27, relayed. MECHANISM: `tools/nativefrontend/buildheader.go` ports go/build's `parseFileHeader` and the line choice of `shouldBuild` (`deps/go/src/go/build/build.go`) — a leading UTF-8 BOM dropped, the comment header read line by line, a `//go:build` line outside a `/* */` comment controls and every `+build` line is then ignored, else the `+build` lines of the leading `//` run before the last blank line count and one that does not parse is prose — as `honouredConstraintLines`, the ONE header reader of both policy sites: `langversion.go` `judgeSelectedFileConstraints` (the selected files, over the bytes `fileselect.go` now reads once for the parser and the judge; a custom-tags-only line that is FALSE there is refused as a disagreement between the port and go/build's own verdict, never as «the oracle would compile without this file») and `fileselect.go` `refuseIgnoredFileConstraints` (the excluded files; the policy's refusal of a custom-tag-excluded file now reaches a BOM-led `//go:build ignore`, which the textual scan stopped at). The policy itself — reserved tag refuses, custom-only false refuses, inert accepted — is unchanged.)
- Pinned-by: differential
- Cases: source-selection/sweep-s20-plusbuild-under-gobuild, source-selection/sweep-s20-plusbuild-in-block
- Discovered: 2026-10-27 by the S20 sweep (lane `sweep/s20-admission`, the defect-neighbourhood campaign's step 2, `docs/2026-10-27_defect-neighbourhood-campaign.md` §4; probes a13, a14, a15, a16b), probing the `+build` legacy form beside the `//go:build` form on BUG-155's axis. Entry: [AGENT] lane worker, 2026-10-27.
- Neighbourhood: found by the S20 sweep (the shape's matrix, extent and classes are on BUG-155's Neighbourhood line); the fix lane probed every branch of go/build's header reader both sides (gc go1.26.5 under the runners' pins; the lane's probes a12–a24 and h1–h13, 2026-10-27): the four fixed shapes, a `//go:build` line inside a `/* */` block (ignored: included on both sides, refused before), after a block (honoured), after a `+build` line and a blank line (it wins), indented (honoured), two of them (go/build's own error), a `+build` line followed by a doc line then a blank (honoured), by a blank then a doc line (honoured), an empty `// +build` and an unparseable `// +build a&&b` (honoured by go/build: excluded on both sides, refused by name), a reserved tag in an ignored placement (prose on both sides, refused before), a leading BOM before an inert `+build` line and before a reserved `//go:build` line (the BOM stripped), and the same shapes in a NAME-excluded file (`x_windows.go`: a `+build` line go/build ignores there is prose and the file drops silently; refused before with a false claim). Pins: `langversion_test.go` `TestBuildConstraintRefusal` (25 shapes) and `TestHonouredConstraintLinesAgreeWithGoBuild` (27 header shapes: the port's honoured lines reproduce go/build's `MatchFile` verdict under the pinned context), `fileselect_test.go` (the excluded-file site, both directions). Not rowable through the differential oracle: the harness re-prints every file through go/printer, which synchronizes build-constraint comments (gofmt's rule since Go 1.17 — a lone `+build` line gains a `//go:build` twin at the top; a `+build` line under a `//go:build` line is rewritten to match it), so a row whose meaning rests on a `+build` line's placement does not reach gc as written: the rows `sweep-s20-plusbuild-no-blank` and `sweep-s20-plusbuild-after-block` were RETIRED by the fix lane (the oracle's copy is excluded where the row's file is included — an apparatus observation for the owner, recorded here and in the baseline header), `sweep-s20-plusbuild-under-gobuild` is kept with its oracle-side `+build` line rewritten to the `//go:build` line's expression (its frontend side exercises the shape as written), `sweep-s20-plusbuild-in-block` is exercised as written on both sides.

WHAT: go/build decides a file's inclusion (`deps/go/src/go/build/build.go` `shouldBuild` / `parseFileHeader`): when a `//go:build` line is present it controls and every `// +build` line is ignored; otherwise `+build` lines count only inside the leading run of `//` comments and blank lines, which ends at the last blank line before the first line that is not a `//` comment (a `/* */` block ends the run, and so does the package clause when no blank line precedes it). The frontend's file SET already comes from go/build under the pinned target (fileselect.go, BUG-108), so on all four shapes the file is INCLUDED on both sides. The standing constraint policy (`tools/nativefrontend/langversion.go` `refuseBuildConstrainedFiles`, the loop over every comment group before `f.Package`, and `judgeBuildConstraintLine`) then re-reads the comments by its own rule — every line for which `constraint.IsPlusBuild` holds is parsed and evaluated with all tags false — and a false line refuses: «file … is EXCLUDED by build constraint "// +build ignore" under the pipeline's default (no -tags) context — the oracle would compile without this file …». The claim is false in the four shapes: gc compiled WITH the file (measured: `go run .` prints 2 on each). The result is an over-refusal (status `unsupported`, exit 1, no wire) of a legal program with a reason that misstates gc; no wrong answer follows. The honest shapes are unaffected: a `+build ignore` line go/build honours (a blank line after it, no `//go:build`) excludes the file on both sides and the refusal is correct (probe a12's twin a18/a20 on the `//go:build` form likewise).

MEASURED (gc go1.26.5, GOPATH mode, the positive harness's layout; the frontend at 89ba27c5), `main.go` reading `x` (1) beside `extra.go` whose init sets 2: (a13) `//go:build !sweepfoo` + `// +build ignore`: gc 2, frontend refuses naming the `+build` line; (a14) `// +build ignore` directly followed by `package main`: gc 2, refused; (a15) `/*\n// +build ignore\n*/`: gc 2, refused; (a16b) `/* c */`, blank line, `// +build ignore`, blank line, `package main`: gc 2, refused. Controls (rows `source-selection/sweep-s20-inert-constraints/*`): `// +build !sweepfoo` with a blank line is inert and included on both sides; `//go:build !sweepfoo` likewise.

ROWS: the four rows were born FAIL/frontend-export (the frontend's refusal); the two the oracle harness can carry as written flipped PASS with the fix, the other two were retired (the Neighbourhood line). FIX (2026-10-27, the Status line): the header rule ported from go/build, both sites. FIX CRITERION (as stated by the sweep): judge constraint lines by go/build's header rule (parse the header as `parseFileHeader` does — a `//go:build` line wins, `+build` lines only in the leading run ended by the last blank line — or take the verdict go/build already made for the file and judge only the line it used), keeping the reserved-tag refusal; the same textual scan over EXCLUDED files (`fileselect.go` `refuseIgnoredFileConstraints`) has the mirror problem in the other direction only in wording (an excluded file is excluded by go/build on both sides whatever the scan says). Related, not a defect: that scan stops at the first line not beginning with `//`, so a UTF-8 BOM before `//go:build ignore` in an excluded file (probe a19, row `source-selection/sweep-s20-inert-constraints/bom-ignore-excluded`) skips the policy's refusal and drops the file silently — as gc drops it (go/build strips the BOM): agreement by construction, recorded on BUG-155's Neighbourhood line.

## BUG-217 — a main module whose `module` path — or the lowered directory's import path under it — is a STANDARD-LIBRARY package path (`module fmt`, `module math/bits`, `module math` with the package in `bits/`) or one of gc's reserved names (`cmd`, `std`, `C`) is a program gc REFUSES to build («ambiguous import: found package fmt in multiple modules», «"cmd" is not an importable package», «unknown import path "C"») and the frontend EXPORTED and the machine ANSWERED (7, status ok) [frontend boundary; over-acceptance of a rejected program — the BUG-158 class through the module path's MEANING rather than its grammar; found by the S20 sweep 2026-10-27, lane `sweep/s20-admission`; FIXED 2026-10-27 in lane `frontend/fix-admission-1027` — the main package's import path judged against the pinned GOROOT and gc's reserved names]

- Status: fixed (2026-10-27, lane `frontend/fix-admission-1027`; the campaign plan's rule that a finding is fixed through the normal train, [USER] approved 2026-10-27, relayed. MECHANISM: `tools/nativefrontend/modfile.go` `refuseReservedModulePath`, run by the loader (`load.go` `loadProgram`) on the go.mod governing the lowered directory: the main package's import path is the module path plus the directory's path under the module root (modload's `DirImportPath`, `mainPackagePath`); it refuses, as the `module` class with gc's reason, a path that is a standard-library package of the pinned GOROOT (`gorootSrcDir`: `GOROOT/src/<path>` holds a `.go` entry — `goroot.IsStandardPackage`'s test — under go/build's GOROOT, the one file selection is pinned to; «ambiguous import: found package fmt in multiple modules»), one of the go command's reserved pattern names `std`, `cmd`, `tool`, `work`, `all` (`search.IsMetaPackage`; «is not an importable package»), `C` («unknown import path "C"»), and a module path `go` or `toolchain` (gc's «invalid module path», the synthetic toolchain modules — measured by the fix lane). A replaced case-local module is judged by its require path in the loader, not by its own go.mod's module line (gc accepts a replaced directory whose go.mod declares another path — measured).)
- Pinned-by: none (the witnesses are NEGATIVE-corpus rows `modules/module-path-std-fmt`, `modules/module-path-std-nested` (`module math/bits`), `modules/module-path-cmd` in `baselines/negative-full.tsv`, born FAIL at `frontend-accepts` and PASS at `frontend=module` since the fix; the subdirectory shape — `module math`, the package in `bits/` — is not rowable, since the negative runner enters module mode only on a go.mod in the row's own directory: its pin is `modfile_test.go` `TestModulePathMeaning`; `scripts/check-bugs.sh` reads only the differential baseline.)
- Discovered: 2026-10-27 by the S20 sweep (lane `sweep/s20-admission`, plan §4; probes b16 and the b2 batch), extending BUG-158's grammar axis to what a module path MEANS to the go command. Entry: [AGENT] lane worker, 2026-10-27.
- Neighbourhood: found by the S20 sweep (the matrix is on BUG-155's Neighbourhood line); the fix lane probed the path's meaning both sides (the sweep's b2 batch re-run and the lane's p1–p12, gc go1.26.5 in module mode, 2026-10-27): refused by both — `fmt`, `strings`, `math/bits`, `net/http`, `unsafe`, `internal/abi`, `cmd/go` (a std path under the cmd module root), `cmd`, `std`, `tool`, `work`, `all`, `C`, `go`, `toolchain`; accepted by both — `main`, `test`, `example.com/fmt`, `fmt/v2`, `vendor/x`, `fmt` with the package in `cmd/`, `cmd/x`, `std/x`, `C/x`, and the GOROOT directories without Go files `internal`, `vendor`, `testdata`. Pins: `modfile_test.go` `TestModulePathMeaning` (28 cells).

WHAT: in module mode the go command resolves the main package by its import path, `<module path>/<directory relative to the module root>` (cmd/go/internal/modload, the import resolution of `import.go`): a path that is also a standard-library package is ambiguous between the main module and std (measured for `fmt`, `strings`, `math/bits`, `net/http`, `unsafe`, `internal/abi`, and for `module math` with the lowered directory `bits/`), `cmd` and `std` are the go command's reserved pattern names («is not an importable package»), and `C` is cgo's pseudo-package («unknown import path "C": internal error: module loader did not resolve import»). SITE: `tools/nativefrontend/modfile.go` `case "module"` (the verb switch, `modulePathOK`): the path's SHAPE is validated (non-empty elements of the identifier grammar, no leading or trailing slash) and nothing else; the frontend already holds the pinned GOROOT's package set (`load.go` `isStdlib`, the stdlib importer, which it uses to refuse a case-local directory that shadows a std path) but never compares the module path, nor the lowered directory's path under it, with that set. MEASURED (gc go1.26.5, module mode, GOPROXY=off, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, the pins of `scripts/go-env-pins.sh`; the frontend at 89ba27c5), a valid program under each go.mod: rejected by gc and EXPORTED — `fmt`, `strings`, `math/bits`, `net/http`, `unsafe`, `internal/abi`, `C`, `cmd`, `std`, and `math` with the package in `bits/`; accepted by both — `main`, `test`, `example.com/fmt`, `fmt/v2`, `vendor/x`, and `fmt` with the package in `cmd/` (import path `fmt/cmd`, no std package of that name).

FIX (2026-10-27, the Status line): the loader judges the main package's path by gc's rule. FIX CRITERION (as stated by the sweep): the scanner refuses by name, as the `module` class, a `module` path for which the lowered directory's import path (the module path joined with the directory's path relative to the module root) is a package of the pinned GOROOT or one of `cmd`, `std`, `C` — the three rows PASS; the frontend's own GOROOT package set is the oracle's at the pin. No modelling: the program's meaning is unchanged by the module path, so the refusal is the whole fix.

## BUG-218 — the go.mod scanner's `require`/`exclude` rule refuses a path SHAPE or a non-canonical VERSION with a message attributing to gc a usage error gc does not raise: `require ./x v1.0.0` and `require example.com/x/ v1.0.0` BUILD under gc (x/mod's parser checks the argument count, the version and the major-version agreement, not the path's grammar), and `require example.com/x v1.0` is resolved by gc as a module query, not refused as a usage error — a misnamed over-refusal, fail-closed, no wrong answer [frontend boundary; BUG-158's scanner; found by the S20 sweep 2026-10-27, lane `sweep/s20-admission`]

- Status: open
- Pinned-by: none (gc ACCEPTS the two path shapes for a program that does not import the required module, so no negative row can hold them and no positive row carries a go.mod (BUG-109's reason); the pins are the sweep's probes b12 and b13 (`.tmp` of the lane, re-runnable from this entry's text). The version shapes (`v1.0`, `1.0.0`, `v01.0.0`) are refused by gc only through the apparatus's `GOPROXY=off` («module lookup disabled by GOPROXY=off») — a verdict of the environment, not of gc's grammar — so they are not rowed either.)
- Discovered: 2026-10-27 by the S20 sweep (lane `sweep/s20-admission`, plan §4; probes b12, b13, b14), probing BUG-158's `require` grammar at path and version shapes beyond the train-20 audit's. Entry: [AGENT] lane worker, 2026-10-27.

WHAT: `tools/nativefrontend/modfile.go` `judgeVersionedPath` (the `require`/`exclude` arm of the verb switch): `modulePathOK(path)` false → `usage(form)`; a version outside `semverCanonicalRE` (and not the `+metadata` shape, which has its own text) → `usage(form)`; and `usage` says «… is not `require module/path v1.2.3` — gc refuses the go.mod («usage: require module/path v1.2.3») …». gc's parser (x/mod `modfile/rule.go`, the `require`/`exclude` case) raises that usage error for the argument COUNT only; the path is checked by `module.CheckPath` when a module is resolved, which `go build .` of a program that imports nothing from it never does (measured: `require ./x v1.0.0` and `require example.com/x/ v1.0.0` build and print 7 under GOPROXY=off; `require fmt v1.0.0` too), and a non-canonical version is a query the go command resolves by a lookup (measured: «go.mod:5: module lookup disabled by GOPROXY=off»). The direction is fail-closed throughout (the DC06 ruling, relayed, asked the scanner to refuse what it does not fully validate; an over-refusal of an exotic go.mod gc accepts was accepted there as the fail-closed direction): the finding is the REASON, which names gc for a refusal gc does not make.

FIX CRITERION: the refusal text states the scanner's own rule (the path or version shape is not one it validates) without attributing it to gc, or the rule follows x/mod's parser (arity, version grammar, major agreement) and leaves the path's grammar to the point gc checks it; the probes' texts no longer name gc. [AGENT] 2026-10-27: entered as the lowest-severity finding of the sweep — a message defect on a fail-closed refusal; the owner may strike it or fold it into BUG-158's text.

## BUG-219 — the loader's CASE-LOCAL import resolution admits ANY subdirectory holding non-test `.go` files and mirrors none of cmd/go's resolution rules, so a program gc REFUSES to build is EXPORTED and ANSWERED (1, status ok): an import path with a `vendor` element (`"vendor/lib"`, `"lib/vendor/x"`: «use of vendored package not allowed» / «vendor/lib must be imported as lib»), an `internal` element from outside its tree (`"internal/x"`, `"lib/internal/x"`: «use of internal package … not allowed», GOPATH mode), a `package main` imported under an alias («import "prog" is a program, not an importable package»), and — under a go.mod — a bare path with no `require`/`replace` behind it (`import "lib"` with `lib/`: «package lib is not in std»; `import "vendor"`: GOROOT/src/vendor) [frontend boundary; over-acceptance of a rejected program, the BUG-125/158 class at the import path; found by the S20 sweep 2026-10-27, lane `sweep/s20-admission`; FIXED 2026-10-27 in lane `frontend/fix-admission-1027` — cmd/go's rules mirrored at discovery, GOPATH and module mode]

- Status: fixed (2026-10-27, lane `frontend/fix-admission-1027`; the campaign plan's rule that a finding is fixed through the normal train, [USER] approved 2026-10-27, relayed. The owner may strike this entry as the recorded limit (row 34) — it is entered so that the boundary's false green has a row and a number, per the campaign's rule.

WHAT: gc's backend refuses a function whose frame — the post-escape-analysis locals, the ABI-assigned argument area, or a callee's — reaches `1 << 30` bytes (`pgen.go` `maxStackSize`; the texts «stack frame too large (>1GB): %d MB locals + %d MB args» and «… + %d MB callee»). go/types does not size frames, and `tools/nativefrontend/gclimits.go` mirrors the TYPE-size rules only (channel element, array vs address space, struct and function-argument width against `MaxWidth = 1 << 50`), saying so in its header: the frame rule is a per-function backend rule. MEASURED (gc go1.26.5, GOPATH mode; the frontend at 89ba27c5): `//go:noinline func f(a [1 << 27]int64) int` called with a package-level array — gc «./main.go:4:6: stack frame too large (>1GB): 0 MB locals + 1024 MB args» and, at main, «… + 1024 MB callee»; the struct form — «1088 MB args»; the frontend exports both (the array type is within the address-space limit and the decoder's footprint budget is not consulted for a parameter type), the machine answers the other subject (7). FIX CRITERION: a post-type-check rule over every function's parameter-plus-result width (the ABI argument area; rounded as gc rounds it) and over each call's callee width, refusing at `>= 1 << 30` as a `type-check:`-class rejection with gc's text, beside the size rules of `gclimits.go`; the two rows PASS. The locals half stays unmirrored by construction (escape analysis is gc's) and is unreachable at the pin through declared locals; a later toolchain that raises `MaxStackVarSize` reopens it — a re-pin obligation, recorded here.

- Neighbourhood: found by the S10 sweep (its matrix is on BUG-081/063/056/038); the fix lane probed every arm of the range emitter over a zero-length or nil operand both sides (the lane's z1–z36, gc go1.26.5, 2026-10-27): the `:=` two-variable form, the `=` assign form, the blank key, the key + blank value, the key only and the no-variable form over a nil and a non-nil `*[0]T`; the operand with a call (evaluated once in the two-variable form, not at all in the key-only form); the array VALUE form; a nil `*[1]T` with two variables (panics on both sides, any width); and the element widths 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16 and 24 across basic, pointer, array, struct, interface, slice and named types. Pins: `emit_test.go` `TestRangeZeroLengthArrayPointer` (the value form at nine widths, the assign form, the three index forms, seven refused widths).

WHAT: gc — `var p *[0]int; n := 0; for i, v := range p { n += i + v + 1 }; return n` answers 0 (spec#For_statements: the range over a pointer to array iterates `len` times reading elements through the pointer; at N = 0 there is nothing to read, nil or not); the same for `p := &[0]int{}` and for `for _, v := range p`. The machine — `native-json-run` stops with status `error` before any step: «native lowering: program.funcs[N].body…rhs.x.y: the source local 'v' (declaration 3) is not in scope at this statement — no declaration of that spelling among the enclosing function's params, results and the declarations that precede the statement in its enclosing blocks (B6 c3; the Stage E6a R1 environment); refused by name» — a refusal of the whole wire, so every other function in the package is refused too.

SITE: `tools/nativefrontend/emit.go`, the range emitter's `*types.Pointer` arm: `if valName == "" || arr.Len() == 0 { … coll = <int N>; kindFields["kind"] = "int"; … valName = "" } else { … kind "array-pointer" … }`. The N == 0 branch reuses the index-only desugar (its comment: «The index-only form (and N == 0) never dereferences — a nil pointer iterates fine, N is static») and CLEARS `valName`; but the value variable was already bound (`bind(rs.Value, "$rangeVal", …)`, a declared local the body references), and the emitted range node carries `valVar: null` with no declaration of it, so the body's reads of `v` dangle. The decoder's B6 c3 environment check (`GoLean/NativeToIR.lean`) catches it, fail closed — a visible refusal, never a wrong answer. REACH: every legal program of the shape — a declared `v` must be used (gc: «declared and not used»), so the body always references the dropped local. The ARRAY-VALUE arm (`case *types.Array`) has no such special case and keeps the value variable (the control row). ROUTE: `*[0]T` only, with a value variable (blank key or not); N > 0 is `range/range-array-pointer-nil-value-panic` and `range/range-not-evaluated/*` (green).

FIX (2026-10-27, the Status line): the value form at the widths gc indexes, the refusal by name elsewhere. FIX SHAPE (as stated by the sweep): at N == 0 with a value variable present, emit the value form (`kind: array-pointer`, `len: 0` — zero iterations, no dereference, the value variable declared) and keep the key-only desugar for `valName == ""`; the non-evaluation rule (BUG-076, `rangeNotEvaluated`) is unaffected. Shape S17 (a form the emitter mis-carries), found by the S10 sweep; the three rows flip PASS with the fix and leave this line.

PLAN [AGENT] (not this lane's; a fix lane through the normal train): route `fmt.Errorf`
